strengths: Correct SPAKE2 role separation: initiator uses start_a, joiner uses start_b via startInitiator/startJoiner, with domain-separated identities (agentpair:{sessionId}:initiator|joiner) — this is what makes matching shared keys derivable (wasm/spake2-pake/src/lib.rs:4-44).
No hand-rolled SPAKE2 math in TypeScript; adapter is a thin wrapper over WASM exports (init/start/respond/finish) as specified (pake-adapter.ts).
Cargo.toml uses RustCrypto spake2 0.4 (curve25519-dalek 4.1.3 per Cargo.lock) — no elliptic/bn.js path, and no npm spake2/cpace added to package.json.
Decision doc thoroughly records Option B chosen and Option A (npm spake2 / cpace) rejected with concrete reasons (pake-selection.md).
pretest hook auto-builds the WASM artifact when wasm/pkg is absent, reducing local test friction (package.json:10).
Includes a negative test (mismatched pairing codes -> non-matching keys) beyond the single required interop case (pake-spike.test.ts:24-34).

issues.description: getrandom backend is configured two ways: Cargo.toml pins getrandom 0.2.17 with the "js" feature (resolved in Cargo.lock), while .cargo/config.toml sets rustflags cfg getrandom_backend="wasm_js" which is a getrandom 0.3 mechanism. With 0.2.17 the cfg is inert (functionality comes from the "js" feature) and may trigger an unexpected_cfgs warning. Harmless but inconsistent.

Decision doc states "committed pkg/ output can be used for tests when the toolchain is present," but wasm/pkg/ is not committed (0 files in the tree / commit). Tests therefore require a local Rust + wasm-pack toolchain via the pretest build step. Doc wording is slightly misleading.
PakeSessionHandle does not expose the WASM session free(); cleanup relies on wasm-bindgen's FinalizationRegistry (nodejs target). Acceptable for a spike, but explicit disposal would be more robust.
